title: Trigonometry & Right Triangles
summary: Master trigonometric ratios—sine, cosine, tangent (SOH-CAH-TOA)—and learn how to calculate unknown sides, angles, and real-world distances.
focus: Right-angled triangles, Hypotenuse, Opposite, Adjacent, Sine, Cosine, Tangent, and the Pythagorean Identity.

cues.text: Trigonometry begins with the foundational right-angled triangle. One angle is exactly ninety degrees, and the longest side lying directly opposite this right angle is always called the hypotenuse.

When we select an acute reference angle theta, the other two legs acquire distinct geometric roles: the opposite side facing theta across the triangle, and the adjacent side running directly alongside theta.

Notice how switching to the other acute angle flips the opposite and adjacent legs, whereas the hypotenuse remains permanently anchored across the ninety-degree right corner. Always verify your reference angle first before writing any ratio.

chapters.title: The Primary Ratios: Sine and Cosine

cues.text: The sine ratio measures vertical rise relative to the hypotenuse: sine of theta equals opposite divided by hypotenuse. As theta opens wider from zero to ninety degrees, sine steadily rises from zero up to one.

Conversely, the cosine ratio measures horizontal projection along the base: cosine of theta equals adjacent divided by hypotenuse. At zero degrees cosine starts at full value one, smoothly declining down to zero as theta reaches ninety degrees.

Together, the ordered pair cosine theta and sine theta determine the exact coordinate position on a unit circle, seamlessly connecting static right-triangle geometry to continuous circular waves, oscillations, and alternating currents throughout physics.

chapters.title: Tangent and the SOH-CAH-TOA Memory Tool

cues.text: The third fundamental ratio is tangent: tangent of theta equals opposite over adjacent, which represents the geometric slope or incline steepness of the hypotenuse.
Quick checkpoint pause: which famous three-letter memory word unites all three foundational trigonometric ratios?

Remember the universal mnemonic acronym: S-O-H C-A-H T-O-A. Sine is Opposite over Hypotenuse; Cosine is Adjacent over Hypotenuse; and Tangent is Opposite over Adjacent. Write this rule down as your constant navigation companion.
With SOH-CAH-TOA at hand, knowing just one acute angle and any one side length allows you to solve every missing dimension and angle across the entire triangle with precision.
Applying Pythagoras a squared plus b squared equals c squared reveals the supreme trigonometric identity: sine squared theta plus cosine squared theta always equals exactly one.
Architects, aerospace engineers, satellite navigation systems, and surveyors apply trigonometry daily to measure mountain heights, ocean distances, and satellite orbits without ever climbing them.

notes.title: The Core Trigonometric Ratios (SOH-CAH-TOA)
notes.text: For any acute angle θ in a right-angled triangle, the three primary ratios compare side lengths: Sine = Opposite / Hypotenuse, Cosine = Adjacent / Hypotenuse, and Tangent = Opposite / Adjacent.
notes.equation: sin θ = Opp/Hyp · cos θ = Adj/Hyp · tan θ = Opp/Adj

notes.title: The Fundamental Pythagorean Identity
notes.text: Derived directly from the Pythagorean theorem (a² + b² = c²), dividing all terms by the square of the hypotenuse yields the most famous identity in trigonometry: sin² θ + cos² θ = 1.

notes.title: Special Right Triangle Exact Values
notes.text: 30°-60°-90° and 45°-45°-90° triangles produce exact ratio values: sin(30°) = 1/2, cos(30°) = √3/2, sin(45°) = √2/2, and tan(45°) = 1.

mistake: Don’t mix up Opposite and Adjacent when changing which angle you analyze. The Opposite side is strictly opposite angle θ, while Adjacent is the touching side that is not the hypotenuse.

practice.question: In a right triangle with angle θ, if Opposite = 3 and Hypotenuse = 5, what is sin(θ) and what is the Adjacent side length?
practice.answer: sin(θ) = 3/5 = 0.6. By Pythagoras (c² = a² + b²), Adjacent = √(5² - 3²) = √(25 - 9) = √16 = 4.
